summary: When blindness and deafness are both timed troubles, apply.c use_unicorn_horn shuffles their list before deciding which one to cure. C calls rnd.c shuffle_int_array; JS records that call as unported and proceeds directly to the cure-count roll, so the cure order and RNG stream diverge.

source.branch: When the uncursed or blessed horn finds more than one timed property trouble, use_unicorn_horn shuffles trouble_list before it rolls val_limit.
callers: apply.c:doapply calls use_unicorn_horn for a unicorn horn.
cmd.c:doturn calls use_unicorn_horn with a null object when a unicorn uses its special ability.
dependencies: rnd.c:shuffle_int_array; the helper mutates the trouble list and consumes rn2 calls

evidence: The admitted v64 manifest identifies apply.c:use_unicorn_horn -> rnd.c:shuffle_int_array and states that the selected case has timed blindness and deafness; C first calls rn2(2), then rolls the number of troubles to cure.
Read nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:2259-2392 and rnd.c:299-310. shuffle_int_array performs the descending Fisher-Yates loop and skips swaps when rn2(i + 1) returns i.

At examined commit 522b8f0, js/apply.js:3610-3612 calls recordGap('rnd.c shuffle_int_array') before immediately drawing valLimit. The first mismatch is step 103, key o: C records rn2(2)=0 (with stale caller exercise(attrib.c:509)); JS instead calls d(2,4)=5 and displays the troubles in reverse order. See .cache/B-v64-horn-before.log.

The saved accepted v64 evaluation reports 119/120 screens, 2447/2454 RNG calls, and 120/120 cursors for this case. The source owner is apply.c and its RNG helper is rnd.c; the queue's attrib.c annotation is not the owning branch.
